gened_codes.FQ: Foundations: Quantitative Reasoning (replaced Foundations: Symbolic Reasoning, "FS", starting Fall 2018)
gened_codes.FG: Foundations: Global & Multicultural Perspectives (6 cr across two courses; note 1 on the sheet). Two FG slots of 3 cr each appear on the grid.
gened_codes.W/WI: Writing Intensive. 5 courses required, minimum of 2 in upper division (note 4). Grid shows 'W Focus (5)'.
gened_codes.H/HAP: Hawaiian, Asian & Pacific Issues. One course required (note 5). Not included in engineering courses -- may double-count with the DH/DL or DS requirement, or be taken standalone (note 6). Grid shows 'H Focus (1)'.
gened_codes.O/OC: Oral Communication. One course required (note 5). Grid shows 'O Focus (1)'.
gened_codes.E/ETH: Contemporary Ethical Issues. One course required (note 5). Grid shows 'E Focus (1)'.

substitutions: MATH 251A, MATH 252A, and MATH 253A (the Accelerated Calculus sequence) may substitute for the MATH 241-244 sequence -- a whole-sequence substitution, not a course-by-course one (note 2).
CHEM 181/181L, or CHEM 171/171L, may substitute for CHEM 161/161L and CHEM 162 (note 3). The sheet doesn't specify whether this is a full 3-for-3 substitution or partial; recorded as printed.
ENGR 196, ENGR 296, and ENGR 396 may substitute for ECE 196, ECE 296, and ECE 396 respectively (note 10).

technical_electives.rule: ECE courses numbered 300 or above, totaling 7 additional credits drawn from the track lists (note 9). Of these, 3 credits must be outside the student's chosen major track and 1 credit must be a laboratory. On the grid: TE ECE (3 cr, Junior Spring) + TE ECE (3 cr) + (Lab) TE ECE (1 cr) (both Senior Fall) = 7 cr, matching note 9.

engineering_breadth.rule: Engineering Breadth (EB, 3 cr) is satisfied by a CEE, ME, OE, or BE course at the 300 level or higher; or CEE 270; or a physical/biological/computer science course at the 300 level or higher, which additionally requires approval from the Department's Undergraduate Curriculum Committee (note 8; the approval clause reads as applying only to the science-course option, not to the CEE/ME/OE/BE or CEE 270 options).

concentrations.Biomedical: All Group I courses in either the EP or Systems Track, plus two biomedical-related Group II courses and an EB course approved by the Department's Undergraduate Curriculum Committee and listed on the ECE website. ECE 496 will be a biomedical project approved by the concentration coordinator.
concentrations.Energy: All Group I courses in either the EP or Systems Track, plus two energy-related Group II courses and an EB course approved by the Department's Undergraduate Curriculum Committee and listed on the ECE website. ECE 496 will be an energy project approved by the concentration coordinator.

other_rules.major_track_minimum: A minimum of 17 credits in one of the major tracks: all track core courses (Group I) plus the remaining track elective courses (Group II).
other_rules.all_courses_letter_graded: ALL COURSES MUST BE TAKEN FOR LETTER (A-F) GRADES.
other_rules.prereq_grade_requirement: Enrollment in ECE courses requires a grade of 'C' or better in all prerequisite courses (note 7).
other_rules.alternate_track_proposal: A student, along with a faculty member, may propose an alternate track if (1) equivalent in rigor & breadth to the listed tracks, (2) endorsed by another faculty member, and (3) approved by the Department's Undergraduate Curriculum Committee (note 11).

known_ambiguities: Note 9's '3 must be outside the major track' most likely means 3 credits (parallel to '1 [credit] must be a laboratory'), not 3 courses, but the sheet doesn't say so explicitly.

ECE 205 is listed as TE-eligible (note 9) despite being below the stated '300 or above' threshold for Technical Electives -- this is an inconsistency in the department's own check sheet, confirmed against the 2026 sheet's identical wording, not a transcription error.
CHEM 171/171L or CHEM 181/181L vs. CHEM 161/161L + CHEM 162: the sheet doesn't specify if this is a full-scope or partial substitution.
